fields.label: Rule Name
fields.description: How this rule is referred to when somebody asks why an order is sitting unapproved. Write it as the sentence you would say: large orders in the south go to the RM.

fields.label: Priority
fields.description: Lower runs first, matching the scheme engine so nobody has to hold two opposite conventions in their head. The first matching rule claims the order.

fields.label: Which Orders
fields.description: Leave a field blank to mean everywhere. Territory is matched down the tree, so a rule set on North covers a shop in North / Delhi / South Delhi.

fields.label: Territory
fields.description: Matched against the whole branch beneath it, never by name equality. Take care setting this in Desk: Frappe fills an empty link from the session default, so a rule that looks unscoped can silently be pinned to whatever territory the person saving it happened to carry.

fields.label: Outlet Class
fields.description: An order worth watching at a D-class shop is unremarkable at an A-class one, so the threshold below usually differs by class rather than being one number for everybody.

fields.label: What Triggers It
fields.description: A rule needs at least one trigger. Without one it would match every order in its scope, and an approval queue that holds everything gets approved without being read.

fields.label: On Order Value
fields.description: Turn the value threshold on. It needs its own switch because a Currency column is zero when nothing was ever typed, and a zero threshold left unset would pull in every order ever booked.

fields.label: Order Value Over
fields.description: Grand total at or above this figure needs approval.

fields.label: On Discount Percent
fields.description: Turn the discount ceiling on, for the same reason the value threshold has a switch: unset and zero are the same stored number, and they mean opposite things here.

fields.label: Discount Percent Over
fields.description: Total discount above this share of gross needs approval. Schemes stack, and two legitimate offers on one cart can land well past what anybody intended to give away.

fields.label: On Credit Breach
fields.description: Catch every order that took the distributor past their limit. The order is still booked at the counter and routed here afterwards - refusing it in front of the shopkeeper does not collect the outstanding, it just costs the sale.

fields.label: Who Approves
fields.description: Whoever is named here may decide these orders and is told when one arrives. They are an addition, not a replacement: the rep's own manager, the distributor and an administrator can still decide, so an order never sits because the named approver is on leave. A role reaches whoever is covering today; a named user is a single point of failure the day they take leave. Prefer the role and name a user only where the decision genuinely belongs to one person.
